summary: Per-frame camera snapshot cache: copies the active camera rig's transform, four sub-camera states and target data out of the field camera controller (gameWork->ctx->f_80) into five embedded publisher blocks, each with its own vtable and a pending byte that Camera_Work_Update flushes through vtable slot +8.
evidence: Camera_Work_Snapshot (0x003DF0D0) reads Os_GetGameWork()->f_08->f_80 and copies the camera transform (source node +0x38..+0x5C), four sub-camera bytes and four positions into self; Camera_Work_Update (0x003DF2C0) then calls vtable slot +8 of the blocks at +0xC/+0x58/+0x84/+0xB0/+0xDC and clears the pending bytes at +0x1C/+0x68/+0x94/+0xC0/+0xEC. Size raised from 244 to 288 because the 4x12-byte position array at +0xF0 ends at +0x120. The type name CameraWork is already used by the 0x001Dxxxx camera work-list signatures for a different object.

fields.name: transformVtable
fields.evidence: Camera_Work_Update does ldr r0,[self+0xC]; ldr r1,[r0+8]; blx r1 with r0=self+0xC, so +0xC is the vtable word of an embedded publisher block that spans +0xC..+0x58

fields.name: isTransformPending
fields.evidence: set to 1 by Camera_Work_Snapshot whenever the transform block changed and cleared to 0 by Camera_Work_Update right after it flushes the block through vtable slot +8

fields.name: maybe_cameraValue
fields.evidence: maybe_cameraValue: Snapshot copies the source node's +0x04 word here and first moves the old value to +0x24, so it is a scalar whose change is detected; the source node is [cameraController+0xD0][0]+0x26C

fields.name: maybe_previousCameraValue
fields.evidence: maybe_previousCameraValue: receives the old +0x20 value on every snapshot (str r1,[r0] after ldr r1,[r0,#-4])

fields.name: transformMatrix00
fields.evidence: first of nine consecutive floats copied verbatim from the source node +0x38..+0x5C into +0x28..+0x48 (ldr [sb,#0x38] then vldmia sb+0x3C {s0..s7}); a 3x3 matrix block, row/column order not proven

fields.name: transformMatrix01
fields.evidence: second float of the 3x3 matrix block copied from source node +0x3C

fields.name: transformMatrix02
fields.evidence: third float of the 3x3 matrix block copied from source node +0x40

fields.name: transformMatrix10
fields.evidence: fourth float of the 3x3 matrix block copied from source node +0x44

fields.name: transformMatrix11
fields.evidence: fifth float of the 3x3 matrix block copied from source node +0x48

fields.name: transformMatrix12
fields.evidence: sixth float of the 3x3 matrix block copied from source node +0x4C

fields.name: transformMatrix20
fields.evidence: seventh float of the 3x3 matrix block copied from source node +0x50

fields.name: transformMatrix21
fields.evidence: eighth float of the 3x3 matrix block copied from source node +0x54

fields.name: transformMatrix22
fields.evidence: ninth float of the 3x3 matrix block copied from source node +0x58

fields.name: paramVtable
fields.evidence: vtable word of the second embedded publisher block (+0x58..+0x84); Camera_Work_Update calls its slot +8 when +0x68 is set

fields.name: isParamPending
fields.evidence: set to 1 by Snapshot in the same branch that fills +0x6C/+0x70/+0x74, cleared by Update after the block's vtable slot +8 runs

fields.name: maybe_cameraParamA
fields.evidence: maybe_cameraParamA: Snapshot stores the source node's +0x14 word here; nothing in the two recovered methods constrains its meaning

fields.name: maybe_cameraParamB
fields.evidence: maybe_cameraParamB: Snapshot stores uVar10, which is the source node's +0x3C word (the second float of the transform matrix), so this is a duplicate of transformMatrix01

fields.name: maybe_cameraParamFlag
fields.evidence: maybe_cameraParamFlag: Snapshot copies the source node's +0x1C byte here

fields.name: subCameraVtable
fields.evidence: vtable word of the third embedded publisher block (+0x84..+0xB0); Update calls its slot +8 when +0x94 is set

fields.name: isSubCameraPending
fields.evidence: set to 1 by Snapshot before the four-sub-camera loop, cleared by Update after the block's vtable slot +8 runs

fields.name: previousSubCameraStates
fields.evidence: Snapshot's loop keeps the previous value of each sub-camera byte here: [0x95+idx] = old [0x99+idx], then [0x99+idx] = node+0x29 and [0x9D+idx] = node+0x5D, for idx 0..3

fields.name: stateVtable
fields.evidence: vtable word of the fourth embedded publisher block (+0xB0..+0xDC); Update calls its slot +8 when +0xC0 is set

fields.name: isStatePending
fields.evidence: written 1 six times by Snapshot (camera id latch and each of the five state bytes) and cleared by Update after the block's vtable slot +8 runs

fields.name: cameraStateA
fields.evidence: compared with the source's 'state id == 5' test (source +0x13C -> +4 == 5) and rewritten only when it differs

fields.name: cameraStateB
fields.evidence: compared with the source byte at +0x150 and rewritten only when it differs

fields.name: cameraStateC
fields.evidence: compared with the source byte at +0x142 and rewritten only when it differs

fields.name: cameraId
fields.evidence: latched once: if +0xCC < 1 and the source camera (+0x130) exists, Snapshot stores source camera +0x64 here and marks the block pending

fields.name: vectorVtable
fields.evidence: vtable word of the fifth embedded publisher block (+0xDC..+0x120); Update calls its slot +8 when +0xEC is set

fields.name: isVectorPending
fields.evidence: set to 1 by Snapshot before the four-position loop, cleared by Update after the block's vtable slot +8 runs

fields.name: subCameraPositions
fields.evidence: four vec3 positions: Snapshot's loop calls 0x0063394C(&vec, cameraController+0x10, idx) and stores the 3 floats at +0xF0+idx*0xC for idx 0..3, so the block ends at +0x120 and the object is at least 288 bytes

summary: Field camera pose record: holds the eye position, the followed target position, a fixed up vector and a smoothed fade value, embeds a Gfx_ScreenFade record at +0xE0 and four Path occlusion sets at +0x160..+0x1FC, and is updated once per frame by Camera_Field_Update.
evidence: Camera_Field_Update (0x0059A4B4) reads the target position/rotation from the camera controller, runs Gfx_ScreenFade_Update on self+0xE0, Camera_UpdateObstructionBlend and maybe_Camera_ComputeViewTransform, then writes the eye position (+0x04..+0x0C), target position (+0x10..+0x18), a constant vector (+0x1C..+0x24) and the smoothed value at +0x28. Camera_Field_Delete (0x0059A814) installs the vtable, calls Ui_MotionPath_Release/Ui_MotionPath_Dtor on the same object (so the class shares the motion-path layout at +0x91/+0xA4..+0xB8) and destroys the four Path objects at +0x160/+0x188/+0x1B0/+0x1D8.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Camera_Field_Delete stores the class vtable (literal 0x0077E254, slots at 0x0077E258: 0x0059A814 Delete, 0x0059A4B4 Update) as the first word

fields.name: cameraPosZ
fields.evidence: Camera_Field_Update writes DAT_0059a5f4[2] + local_38 here; +0x04/+0x08 receive the X/Y components of the same eye position but were not recorded as fields in this batch

fields.name: targetPosX
fields.evidence: written as *pfVar1 + local_34 where local_34 comes from Menu_Cursor_GetPosition(cameraController+0x10), i.e. the followed target's position

fields.name: targetPosY
fields.evidence: second component of the target position (pfVar1[1] + fStack_30)

fields.name: targetPosZ
fields.evidence: third component of the target position (pfVar1[2] + fStack_2c)

fields.name: maybe_upVectorX
fields.evidence: maybe_upVectorX: copied every update from the constant vector at 0x007E7024 (DAT_0059a5f8); a fixed 3-float vector, the up axis is the most plausible reading but is not proven

fields.name: maybe_upVectorY
fields.evidence: maybe_upVectorY: second word of the constant vector at 0x007E7024

fields.name: maybe_upVectorZ
fields.evidence: maybe_upVectorZ: third word of the constant vector at 0x007E7024

fields.name: smoothedFadeValue
fields.evidence: self +0x28 += (fade+0x24 * DAT_0059a5fc - self+0x28) * DAT_0059a600, i.e. an exponential smoothing of a value taken from the embedded screen-fade record

fields.name: isActive
fields.evidence: Camera_Field_Update returns immediately unless this byte is non-zero; Ui_MotionPath_Release (called from Camera_Field_Delete) clears it

fields.name: screenFade
fields.evidence: Gfx_ScreenFade_Update(self+0xE0) is called every frame and maybe_Camera_ComputeViewTransform also takes self+0xE0 as its parameter block; Gfx_ScreenFade is 96 bytes so the record spans +0xE0..+0x140

fields.name: screenFadeBlend
fields.evidence: read as the target of the +0x28 smoothing; it is the +0x24 float of the embedded Gfx_ScreenFade at +0xE0, so it is named here only because the batch recorded it as a Camera_Field offset

fields.name: occlusionPath0Vtable
fields.evidence: first of four 0x24-byte Path objects at +0x160/+0x188/+0x1B0/+0x1D8; Camera_Field_Delete passes each to Container_ReleaseListAndFree (the Path deleting destructor) and Path_Dtor, and Camera_UpdateObstructionBlend picks one of the four sets by the field-mode byte

fields.name: occlusionPath0Valid
fields.evidence: cleared right after the Path at +0x160 is destroyed (strb r5,[r6,#0x24] with r6 = self+0x15C), i.e. the +0x20 byte of that Path object

fields.name: occlusionPath1Vtable
fields.evidence: vtable word of the second Path object at +0x188

fields.name: occlusionPath1Valid
fields.evidence: the +0x20 byte of the Path object at +0x188, cleared after its destruction

fields.name: occlusionPath2Vtable
fields.evidence: vtable word of the third Path object at +0x1B0

fields.name: occlusionPath2Valid
fields.evidence: the +0x20 byte of the Path object at +0x1B0, cleared after its destruction

fields.name: occlusionPath3Vtable
fields.evidence: vtable word of the fourth Path object at +0x1D8

fields.name: occlusionPath3Valid
fields.evidence: the +0x20 byte of the Path object at +0x1D8, cleared after its destruction; the object ends at +0x1FC, which matches the recorded size 508

summary: 56-byte save-code (Spell of Restoration) record: the init stores a 0x303 header, three caller words and a 40-byte payload area, then dispatches on the length of a wide-character password (17 or 20) to the save-code decoders. The Camera_TargetDescriptor name is inherited from the M1 pass and is wrong - nothing here is a camera target.
evidence: 0x003EAA70 stores 0x303 at +0, r6/r12/r3 at +4/+8/+0xC, zeroes +0x10..+0x34, then calls wcslen(name) and branches on the result: length 0x14 -> SaveCode_EncodeFixed20 (0x005EF4F0, requires count == 0x14 and ids in 0x3000..0x30FC), length 0x11 -> 0x005EFE24, and the first time through it also calls Save_Crypto_SetKeyFromString (0x005F0924, Blowfish key schedule). Returns 3 when the name is null or empty, 0 on success. The class name cannot be changed because apply.py resolves it against structs.json.

fields.name: magic
fields.evidence: the init builds it as (self & 0xFFFF0000) | 3 | 0x300 then uxth, i.e. the constant 0x00000303 (byte0 = 3, byte1 = 3)

fields.name: maybe_initArg5
fields.evidence: maybe_initArg5: stored from r6 (a callee-saved incoming argument) by the stm r4,{r1,r6,r12}; nothing in the body constrains its meaning

fields.name: maybe_initArg6
fields.evidence: maybe_initArg6: stored from r12 by the same stm; r12 is not an AAPCS argument register, so the decompiler may have lost the real source

fields.name: maybe_initArg4
fields.evidence: maybe_initArg4: stored from r3 (the fourth argument) before the name is examined

fields.name: payloadWord0
fields.evidence: first of ten words zeroed by the init (+0x10..+0x34, 40 bytes); the record is then filled from a wide-character password by the save-code decoders, so this is the payload area

fields.name: payloadWord1
fields.evidence: second payload word, zeroed by the init

fields.name: payloadWord2
fields.evidence: third payload word, zeroed by the init

fields.name: payloadWord3
fields.evidence: fourth payload word, zeroed by the init

fields.name: payloadWord4
fields.evidence: fifth payload word, zeroed by the init

fields.name: payloadWord5
fields.evidence: sixth payload word, zeroed by the init

fields.name: payloadWord6
fields.evidence: seventh payload word, zeroed by the init

fields.name: payloadWord7
fields.evidence: eighth payload word, zeroed by the init

fields.name: payloadWord8
fields.evidence: ninth payload word, zeroed by the init

fields.name: payloadWord9
fields.evidence: tenth payload word, zeroed by the init; the record ends at +0x38, which matches the recorded size 56

summary: Camera motion-set window: a Ui_Window-derived object (vtable 0x0076B7F0, slot 6 is Ui_Window_LayoutRows) that owns four embedded Ui_Object sub-windows, two intrusive list heads and two record arrays - eight 0xB8-byte track records at +0x528 and twenty-four 0x50-byte slot records at +0xAEC. The same object is also described by the Ui_CameraAnimWindow class entry.
evidence: 0x003ED388 is the destructor, not the constructor the batch labels it as: it stores vtable 0x0076B7F0, calls std_destroy_range(self+0xAEC, 0x004CF57C, 0x50, 0x18) and std_destroy_range(self+0x528, 0x0045F07C, 0xB8, 8), relinks the list heads at +0x514/+0x518 and +0x520/+0x524, then chains Ui_Object_DtorBase on self+0x4BC, self+0x34C, self+0x300 and self+0x2B4 and std_destroy_range(self+0x174, 0x0045F08C, 0x50, 4). 0x003ED378 is the deleting destructor (same body plus free). Size raised from 1324 to 4716 because the 24x0x50 array at +0xAEC ends at +0x126C.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: the teardown at 0x003ED388 stores the literal 0x0076B7F0 as the first word; that vtable's slots are 0x003ED388 (destructor), 0x003ED378 (deleting destructor), 0x003EC23C, 0x003EC6CC, 0x001D89B4 Ui_Window_LayoutRows, 0x003ECDB0

fields.name: uiObjectVtable
fields.evidence: Ui_Object_DtorBase (0x001A6768) is called on self+0x4BC, so an embedded Ui_Object base starts there and this is its vtable word; the same teardown then relinks the list heads at +0x4A8/+0x4B4 of that sub-object

fields.name: listOwnerVtable
fields.evidence: set to the constant 0x00759388 (a vtable whose first slot is 0x001A5FE8) and immediately followed by the relinking of two intrusive list heads at +0x514/+0x518 and +0x520/+0x524, so an embedded list-owning object starts here

fields.name: list0Next
fields.evidence: first word of the intrusive list head at +0x514: the teardown does [head+4] = head and [head+8] = head, the standard empty-ring initialisation

fields.name: list0Prev
fields.evidence: second word of the same intrusive list head at +0x518

fields.name: list1Next
fields.evidence: first word of the second intrusive list head at +0x520

fields.name: list1Prev
fields.evidence: second word of the second intrusive list head at +0x524

fields.name: trackRecords
fields.evidence: std_destroy_range(self+0x528, 0x0045F07C, 0xB8, 8) destroys eight 0xB8-byte records starting here, so the array spans +0x528..+0xAE8; the element type is not recovered, hence the opaque byte array

summary: Periodic camera-shake work object: a Container_NameHash named 'ReguralyShake' that lives in the camera named map at gameWork->ctx->f_78 and spawns a Gfx_MoveNode shake node every shakePeriod seconds, carrying the three node parameters and the node slot.
evidence: Camera_RegularShake_Ctor (0x0059131C) calls Container_NameHash_Ctor(self, "ReguralyShake"), stores five float arguments at +0x7C/+0x80/+0x84/+0x88/+0x8C and the slot byte at +0x90, then installs vtable 0x0077D85C. Camera_CreateRegularShakeWork (0x0059121C) allocates exactly 0x94 = 148 bytes for it and inserts it into the named map at ctx+0x78. Camera_RegularShake_Update (0x005912C0) counts +0x80 down by the frame delta and calls 0x0046B40C(slot, x, y, z) when it expires.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Camera_RegularShake_Ctor stores the literal 0x0077D85C as the first word after Container_NameHash_Ctor has built the base

fields.name: maybe_isFinished
fields.evidence: maybe_isFinished: Camera_RegularShake_Update sets it to 1 when the period at +0x7C is <= 0.0 and nothing in this class reads it; it lies inside the 124-byte Container_NameHash base, whose constructor zeroes it

fields.name: shakePeriod
fields.evidence: compared with 0.0 at the top of the update (vcmpe s2,s1 with s1 = 0.0) and used as the reload value for the countdown at +0x80 (ldr r0,[r4,#0x7c]; str r0,[r4,#0x80])

fields.name: shakeTimer
fields.evidence: counted down by the frame delta (vsub.f32 s0,s2,s0; vstr s0,[r4,#0x80]) and reset to +0x7C when it reaches zero

fields.name: maybe_shakeParam0
fields.evidence: maybe_shakeParam0: first of the three floats loaded with vldmia r4+0x84 {s0,s1,s2} and passed to the shake-node factory 0x0046B40C, which stores them at node +0x80/+0x84/+0x88; the factory's own field meanings are not proven

fields.name: maybe_shakeParam1
fields.evidence: maybe_shakeParam1: second of the three floats handed to 0x0046B40C (node +0x84)

fields.name: maybe_shakeParam2
fields.evidence: maybe_shakeParam2: third of the three floats handed to 0x0046B40C (node +0x88)

fields.name: shakeSlot
fields.evidence: loaded with ldrb r0,[r4,#0x90] and passed as the first argument of 0x0046B40C, which stores it as the node's mode byte at +0x8C; the constructor takes it as its second argument
